name: Question 1
problem: Consider the portion of the surface $z=\operatorname{sin}⁡x+y$ whose projection onto the $xy$-plane is bounded by the curve $y=\sqrt{4-{x}^{2}},$ and the $x$-axis. Find a repeated integral expression for the surface area of this surface.
worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ defined by $z=f(x,y)$ with $(x,y)\in D,$ the surface area of $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}\sqrt{1+{(\frac{∂z}{∂x})}^{2}+{(\frac{∂z}{∂y})}^{2}}\,\text{d}A.
$$

In this case, our surface is given by

$$
z=\operatorname{sin}⁡x+y,\,(x,y)\in D
$$

where the region $D$ is given by

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,-2\le x\le 2,\,0\le y\le \sqrt{4-{x}^{2}}},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14071034/assets/8bf7a5921936b44a2e672fcee524c5a230800e6130f6c0a8683e6ce46829df58.png)

Now, since

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂z}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\operatorname{sin}⁡x+y)=\operatorname{cos}⁡x, \\ \frac{∂z}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(\operatorname{sin}⁡x+y)=1,\end{aligned}
$$

the surface area is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}\,\text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}\sqrt{1+{(\frac{∂z}{∂x})}^{2}+{(\frac{∂z}{∂y})}^{2}}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\sqrt{1+(\operatorname{cos}⁡x)^{2}+(1)^{2}}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\sqrt{2+{cos}^{2}⁡x}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{-2}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{4-{x}^{2}}}\sqrt{2+{cos}^{2}⁡x}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 1

Consider the portion of the surface z=sin⁡x+y whose projection onto the xy-plane is bounded by the curve y=4−x2, and the x-axis. Find a repeated integral expression for the surface area of this surface.

a
∫−22∫04−x22+cos⁡xdydx
b
∫−22∫04−x21+sin⁡x+ydydx
c
∫−22∫04−x21+4cos2⁡xdydx
d
∫−22∫04−x22+cos2⁡xdydx
e
∫−22∫04−x21+sin2⁡x+y2dydx
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

For a surface S defined by z=f(x,y) with (x,y)∈D, the surface area of S is given by

∬SdS=∬D1+(∂z∂x)2+(∂z∂y)2dA.

In this case, our surface is given by

z=sin⁡x+y,(x,y)∈D

where the region D is given by

D={(x,y):−2≤x≤2,0≤y≤4−x2},

as shown in the diagram below.

Now, since

∂z∂x=∂∂x(sin⁡x+y)=cos⁡x,∂z∂y=∂∂y(sin⁡x+y)=1,

the surface area is given by

∬SdS=∬D1+(∂z∂x)2+(∂z∂y)2dA=∬D1+(cos⁡x)2+(1)2dA=∬D2+cos2⁡xdA=∫−22∫04−x22+cos2⁡xdydx.
